fix.note: Partly closed. The security gate now judges a change by what it ADDED, not by the whole file. BLOCKING (High), from gates/manifest_delta.ts: a git, GitHub-shorthand or tarball-URL dependency in package.json; an added or changed preinstall, install or postinstall script; a changed `registry=` line in .npmrc. ADVISORY (Medium): a path or link dependency; an added or raised version override; and, from security/dep_delta.ts, every dependency a change adds or raises in package.json, package-lock.json or requirements.txt, reported as 'Dependency Check': NOT checked for known vulnerabilities, with the names. A version range or a non-registry source cannot name an installed version, so it is listed as not checkable from the manifest. The gate takes an optional synchronous advisory source (options.advisoryLookup): a pair it answers with ids becomes a non-blocking 'Known Vulnerability' finding; a source that returns undefined or throws leaves the pair 'not checked', never clean. purix check, modify and ingest print a line that says not checked is not a clean result. Tests: 30 in security_gate_dependency_delta.test.ts (22 of the first 28 failed on the old code), 18 in security_gate_f0302.test.ts (all failed before: module missing), 3 in verify/surface_text.test.ts. A plain `npm audit` after the change was rejected: the sandbox does not install, so it would audit the old lockfile and report the new dependency clean. Merge note: the two sessions built the same advisory twice; the merged gate keeps the blocking rules from the patch session and the 'not checked' advisory, lockfile and requirements.txt reading and the advisory-source hook from the other, so one added dependency produces one note. (2) D-r: an ordinary advisory is reported and never blocks; a malicious-package record (OSV MAL- id) blocks (High). (3) Lockfiles are judged against their base (gates/lock_delta.ts): a changed or new entry from a git/URL/file source, or from a host no old entry used, or the same version with a different integrity value, is High; a move to one new registry is ONE finding.
